problem: Offer a rigorous degree to many more students at a much lower price.
title: Georgia Tech launches a low-cost online master's degree in computer science
context: Online learning was growing and master's degrees were expensive.
decision_made: Launch an online MS in Computer Science delivered through Udacity, with AT&T funding, at an approximate cost of $6,600.
action_taken: Launched in January 2014 with about 375 students; 401 were offered admission.
observed_outcome: After ten years the programme reported over 60,000 applications; graduates were reported as over 12,000 in one source and over 10,000 in another. The first graduates finished in less than two years.
lessons: A lower-cost online degree can scale without immediately hurting quality, with partners paying for the build.
limitations: Figures are programme-reported, and graduate counts differ between sources. Cost figures changed over time, and a $7,000 figure was not confirmed.

claims.claim_text: Georgia Tech, Udacity and AT&T launched an online MS in Computer Science in January 2014.
The programme reports over 10,000 graduates in its 2024 annual report.
